### [88] VERIFIED
Verbatim confirmed: "Brake is only on the RA axis, and is a spring loaded solenoid brake such that when there is power, the solenoid is active and allows the stepper to rotate, and when power is off, the solenoid is deactivated and the brake is pushed in place."; "Belt failure" in the what-if list followed by "there could be situation where the lock is off and the load could freewheel"; "DEC axis has no braking, however provided the scope/imaging train is center balanced... it's unlikely to move on it's own"; test: "with 14lb of gear and placed the RA in the worst position on left and right. Powered off and the load didn't fall. Pushing on it, it moved and it kept going for a few seconds... Thereʼs a reduction gear behind it, so it will never drop fast, but if thereʼs enough weight it will keep going till it hits the tripod/pier extension". Both axes have home sensors (infrared beam interruption). "Stall detection" is jetty's remark about cold-weather DEC stops ("The stepper drivers have stall detection, and I suspect they are using it"), correctly characterised as a guess.
Note: the omitted sentence "14lb is about the limit where if there is no brake, there could be issues" is relevant context; the docs' "did not fall by itself" is accurate but the 14 lb figure is the author's stated limit, not a safe margin.
